# OpenAI Dart Client

> Dart client for the OpenAI API with Responses API, Decisions API, Chat Completions, images, videos, audio, custom tools, embeddings, evals, realtime, signed webhooks, safety retrieval, structured monitoring errors, and more.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/README.md) (~11.8k tokens): Primary package documentation with installation, configuration, and usage examples.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/CHANGELOG.md) (~27.2k tokens): Release history and version-by-version changes.
- [MIGRATION](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/MIGRATION.md) (~24.2k tokens): Upgrade notes and breaking-change guidance.
- [Monitoring failures](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/README.md#how-do-i-inspect-monitoring-failures): Shared passive HTTP/failed Response/WS details, flat nullable SSE errors, scoped investigation and migration boundaries.
- [HTTP/2 transport evaluation](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/specs/api-alignment/reviews/46-http2.md) (~3.1k tokens): Local TLS compatibility and matched benchmark evidence; defer experimental native adapter adoption, with no production transport change.

## Voice consent management

client.audio.voiceConsents is cached and supports create/list/retrieve/update/delete with abort, shared auth and conservative retries. Create is a three-field multipart upload with immutable recording bytes, filename and optional normalized MIME metadata; eight supported bases and 10 MiB limit. Update is required-name JSON POST. List only accepts after/limit and fetches one page; cursor presence distinguishes omission/null/value. Closed canonical responses preserve immutable receive-only future extras; deleted false remains false. Private default diagnostics/logs retain explicit caller error/HTTP context. Eligible project/access, api.voices.write and the current consent phrase are service requirements; recordings/sample must come from the same person/project. Sample-derived voice creation is available through client.audio.voices.create; no undocumented consent_phrases DTO is invented.

## Custom voice creation

client.audio.voices.create accepts VoiceCreateRequest: the existing CustomVoiceCreateRequest for consent/sample multipart uploads, or PromptVoiceCreateRequest(name,prompt,scriptHint?,model?) with fixed type prompt. Prompt creation defaults to JSON and also supports encoding: VoiceCreateEncoding.multipart; samples require multipart and preserve omitted type/audio_sample plus immutable bytes/MIME. Name is 1–256 Unicode code points; prompt/scriptHint 1–2000 and nonblank. Optional fields stay omitted; service defaults/model and script shortness remain service-owned. Creation is sent once to avoid duplicate saved voices after uncertain delivery.

CustomVoice.type distinguishes prompt/audio_sample; optional original prompt is nonnull when supplied. Retain that description and select LiveVoice.custom(id: voice.id) at Live startup. Prompt voices support Live only, not Speech/Realtime/Chat audio; creation returns metadata without preview audio. All nine announced named Live voices already have constants, and LiveVoice.named preserves future names. delete(id) explicitly deletes the saved voice (not its consent), retaining deletedfalse and fixed audio.voice.deleted metadata. Default logs/errors redact IDs, prompts, headers and payloads; explicit caller context remains readable.

- [prompt_voices_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/prompt_voices_example.dart): Offline prompt create/Live configuration/delete, two mock requests, no API cost.

## File audio and Chat voices

ChatAudioConfig accepts typed open/custom AudioVoice references and marin/cedar; AAC is appended while pcm16 stays Chat-specific. File transcription already has all 14 form fields; fileContentType is optional file-part MIME metadata. Use gpt-transcribe with plural languages and supported keywords; specialist verbose/subtitle/diarization/English translation modes depend on the model. Translation create is JSON-only, createVerbose accepts canonical responses without task, and createRaw preserves text/SRT/VTT whitespace. Buffered file methods accept abortTrigger; transcription streams complete on valid transcript.text.done without replay. Received metadata/bytes/collections are immutable and private automatic diagnostics are redacted.

The February 26, 2027 Whisper/GPT-4o file-transcription sunset requires workflow-aware migration to gpt-transcribe/gpt-live-transcribe; retain operational specialist outputs until a replacement fits. It is separate from January 6 TTS and January 20 legacy snapshot notices. See README and MIGRATION for widened getters, appended enum cases and removed collection constructor const.

## Realtime input, audio controls and Translation

Import openai_dart_realtime.dart with a prefix alongside the main client. RealtimeConnection.createResponse(input: ...) accepts native RealtimeResponseInputItem references, role-specific messages and function call/output history. References select existing server item IDs and are distinct from full conversation items; GA native input constraints are not the wider retained beta conversation-item contract. Status-details error.message remains available in raw response.created/done payloads. Transcription delta contentIndex/delta can be absent; nullable logprobs and optional obfuscation are retained. Existing DTMF event/received_at stay intact through the raw unknown-event fallback.

AudioInputNoiseReduction and RealtimeTranslationNoiseReduction accept optional strength0..1; validate finite bounds before serialization without inserting default1. Omission on update preserves strength, and clearStrength removes the local field rather than resetting the server. Disable noise reduction through the wrapper's explicit null-clear flag. Translation requires noise type; GA type stays optional. RealtimeAudioConfigOutput.voice remains the named string API; voiceSelection accepts the shared AudioVoice object/string reference, mutually exclusive with voice. Audio-sample custom voices support Realtime; prompt voices support Live only. Session transcription model/languages/keywords already use InputAudioTranscription; returned keywords are unrelated to the ordinary /audio transcription response model.

connect supports optional model, callId and documented intent (realtime/transcription), retaining service-owned target validation and typed query precedence. Model-less secret-selected and transcription connections omit the model query. Reconnect remains limited to model-selected sessions without call_id/intent per the existing Node-compatible admission boundary. Translation retains required model at /realtime/translations and its separate typed continuous event stream; it has no response.create/commit lifecycle. Configure language/source transcription/noise, send raw24kPCM16LEmono including silence, request session.close, consume remaining output through session.closed, then close locally. Cancellation/transport failure never claims successful flush; recovery never restores configuration/audio/history automatically. A scoped secret may be created through realtimeSessions.translations.createClientSecret. Browsers must use WebRTC or authenticated backend proxies; configured WS headers are rejected before credential lookup.

Audio deprecations: January6,2027 legacyTTS→Realtime2.1mini workflow; January20 legacyRealtime/audio→Realtime2.1/mini or Chatgpt-audio-1.5; February26 legacyWhisper/transcribe→gpt-transcribe/gpt-live-transcribe and /audio/translations→RealtimeTranslation. Route migration is required where endpoints differ; model IDs stay open strings. Retained beta codecs do not restore the May12,2026 removed beta service. See official deprecations and MIGRATION.md.

- [realtime_input_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/realtime_input_example.dart): Offline acknowledged history reference and new typed response context.
- [realtime_translation_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/realtime_translation_example.dart): Offline secret/config/noise/transcripts/audio/flush-close flow, zero API or device cost.

## Live HTTP sessions

client.live.sessions is cached and implements create/accept/reject/refer/hangup/fork/downloadRecording/downloadRecordingStream. Canonical create supports WebRTC offers and outbound SIP (E.164 destination, TLS provider URL, Digest auth, caller number), beyond the pinned clients' narrower helpers. SIP 201 means initialized before answer; ambiguous POST timeout/connection/5xx is sent once, and tracing does not deduplicate. Exact 201 JSON/empty 200/WAV response modes, shared auth/abort/errors, opaque encoded IDs and closed-client guards. Content has its own live_ ID pattern and preserves WAV plus 503 Retry-After. Storage defaults false, needs project policy, excludes ZDR; finalized recordings last 30 days. No polling or automatic call actions. Verify live.transport.incoming and use data.sessionId for an explicitly chosen control.

Complete shared startup/media/fork/session/audio/history/frontend/delegation models preserve declared fields, optional/null/absence, copy/clear and finite immutable open JSON. Thirteen distinct Live tool input variants plus nested shell helpers; 12 typed specific choices and allowed_tools 1–128. Service runtime support may be narrower than canonical wire coverage. Startup model/voice/history/audio format/instructions/delegation mode remain immutable; updates change backend settings. PCM16LE at 16/24 kHz and G.711 PCMA/PCMU at 8 kHz are primary-WebSocket formats; WebRTC/SIP omit audio.format. Live custom voice objects are open with IDs of 1–128 characters, independently of Speech's closed custom reference. Default logs/diagnostics redact private wire data; explicit caller models/errors remain readable. Primary/sideband/fork transports, codecs, compact Responses dispatch and transcript helpers are available; opt-in recovery and explicit pending delivery are available; remaining media conveniences stay inventoried.

Outbound SIP creation enforces the documented 1 MiB serialized UTF-8 body limit. The service limits ringing to three minutes and connected calls to two hours; request configuration does not change these durations. Forks reject known inherited model/voice/instructions/history overrides even through raw JSON, while preserving unrelated finite future metadata.

## Live WebSockets

client.live.connect() opens an unstarted primary socket without a model query; start(LiveSessionStartEvent) waits session.started. client.live.attach(id, gracefulClose: ...) attaches without startup/audio submission. Typed primary/sideband/fork codecs preserve command direction and channel admission, including Decisions and audio fixtures; SIP DTMF commands and notifications require a sideband. LiveInputItem covers every declared canonical backend input branch separately from narrower ordinary Responses helpers. Response.event preserves arbitrary finite nested JSON, compact lifecycle snapshots and omission/null delegation IDs. Reflected sideband audio is original mono PCM16LE 24 kHz with output timestamps; keep delivery order/frame gaps. No Realtime commit, implicit reconnect/replay or action runner.

closeSession installs final tracking before sending, blocks new work, drains with caller timeout/abort and confirms only LiveSessionClosed. close() is local transport cleanup; owned sockets close once and borrowed adapters retain ownership. latestUsageSeconds replaces cumulative audio snapshots; keep Responses backend tokens separate. Concurrent taps observe events without owning socket lifetime. Browser defaults reject every configured header before provider auth; use trusted signaling/caller WebRTC channels or explicitly injected proxy adapters. Wrap HTTP-started caller data channels with LivePrimaryConnection(adapter, sessionAlreadyStarted: true, ownsSocket: false), optionally with a known initialSession; duplicate startup/audio append are rejected. No Live ephemeral-key endpoint. Applications own authorization/execution, IDs, deduplication and all function results before one response.create; no item-create success ack.

## Live audio fixtures and SIP DTMF

LiveOutputAudioFixturePlayParam.fromBytes accepts nonempty even raw mono PCM16LE24k samples, at most1,440,000bytes/30seconds; its string constructor preserves valid standardbase64 up to1,920,000characters. Known WAV containers are rejected; no conversion or session-format inference is performed. Headerless bytes cannot prove channel count/rate/endianness. Primary/fork WebSockets and sidebands admit fixtures; borrowed WebRTC data channels reject them. Playing means validated acceptance; Played means server mixer drained/inference resumes, not listener completion. No synthetic played on failure/cancellation/close. One fixture at a time, input during playback is dropped, and instructions/thinking/commentary appends are server-rejected. No guessed local playback state or automatic buffer/replay. Explicit input mute/unmute acknowledgments are independent; fixture emits neither and unmute during fixture does not resume inference before drain. Sideband reflection remains before muting.

LiveTransportDTMFSendParam(event: key, eventId: optional) sends one ASCII0–9/A–D/*/# key on a SIP server sideband; primary/fork/data-channel sends reject it. Generic sideband attachment does not prove SIP: service checks eligibility and emits error with error.clientEventId when supplied. LiveTransportDTMFSent uses transport.dtmf.sent plus optional nonnull clientEventId, confirming trunk submission, not remote IVR success. LiveTransportDTMFReceived is caller-to-session. Removed receive transport.dtmf.send is preserved as finite UnknownLiveServerEvent for saved data. Update exhaustive sealed switches and the old LiveTransportDTMFSend symbol; see MIGRATION.md. All new models are exported by the existing live barrel.

- [live_media_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/live_media_example.dart): Offline fixture acceptance/drain, independent mute and SIP DTMF directions; no API/media/telephony charges.

## Stored Live forks and transcripts

client.live.forkConnection(sourceId) opens the exact stored-session route with no model query or automatic startup. start(LiveForkSessionStartEvent(session: LiveForkSessionConfigParam())) explicitly inherits settings. New fork writers admit only documented root/audio overrides, excluding WebRTC permissions and inherited model/voice/instructions/history; old shared HTTP DTO open metadata is retained. Store requires project policy and non-ZDR; wait for session.closed and recording finalization. New WS format defaults PCM16 24k independently of source. No startup/audio/tool/action replay or automatic backend restoration.

LiveResponsesEvent.fromLiveEvent dispatches sparse lifecycle snapshots via LiveCompactResponse, reuses ordinary granular codecs where source contracts match, and preserves finite future or incompatible child shapes as raw views. Known malformed fields remain errors. The nested type is separate from required outer source.type response.event. Collect all active function calls through backend generation finalization before every output and one explicit continuation; empty compact output/tools is not a pending-call ledger. IDs/canceled outcomes/authorization/execution belong to one application action owner; backend/session/playback lifetimes remain separate.

LiveTranscriptGrouper attaches a non-consuming event tap; complete segment snapshots replace caption text by local ID. SDK grouping defaults are 500/2000/1000/2000 ms plus a 50 ms settle window, with event-ID dedup, timestamp reset, acknowledgments/interruptions and monotonic inactivity fallback. Raw taps remain lossless while grouping can suppress backchannels. Helper closure cancels only its timer/tap; finalized requires observed session.closed. Pure LiveTranscriptGrouping uses explicit source time. projectLiveTranscriptPlayback is an additive Dart caller-clock projection, not SDK hardware playback or audible completion. LiveConnection.dataChannel(callerChannel) is a typed already-started borrowed writer; cleanup never closes caller media/listeners. Opt-in reconnect/unsent queues/escape hatches/media engines remain inventory.

## Decisions image references

DecisionInputPart.image admits exact case-sensitive `data:`, `http://`, `https://` prefixes through constructors/parsers/copies. Strings are preserved, including escapes/query/fragment; the service checks image validity and public accessibility. The client does not fetch or normalize images. imageBytes and omitted detail/auto behavior remain compatible; all four ImageDetail values and 128-image request limit remain. File IDs/unsupported roles/audio/tools stay excluded. Current canonical schema and HTTP reference supersede older inline-only guide/SDK prose. The offline URL example closes its caller-owned mock transport.

## Safety alert explanations

SafetyAlert exposes typed detailedExplanation and hasDetailedExplanation, preserving absent/null/string including empty text. Constructor omission can adopt a valid explanation from legacy rawJson; explicit typed/presence inputs win. copyWith omission preserves, detailedExplanation:null retains a null key and hasDetailedExplanation:false removes it from effective JSON. Known raw values remain validated and cannot override typed values or resurrect cleared keys; finite future JSON is deeply immutable. rawJson retains the detached received snapshot, including an original explanation after effective clear; toJson reflects current typed presence/value. Equality/hash follow complete effective JSON and default diagnostics redact explanation/private metadata. The service determines temporary eligible-ZDR availability; reason:null does not prove eligibility. Existing explicit project GET/scoping remains, with no alert list/control/cache or changed webhook field. The Responses monitoring explanation remains optional nonnull. The offline example closes its caller-owned mock transport.

## Agent context, review and session updates

Saved and inline session Agents use AgentCompactionConfig/AgentCompaction and AgentExperimentalConfig/AgentExperimentalOverridesConfig/AgentExperimental. Request compaction.async is optional nullable; the resolved boolean is required. Omitted/null async selects background compaction. A supplied compaction object replaces the settings; omitted parent updates retain them, and null/{} resets background behavior. Experimental timeAwareness updates merge supplied keys; omission retains the current value, false disables reminders, and wire null is invalid. Do not serialize invented defaults.

SessionReviewParam/Resource support none/auto_review independently of removed spend_control. Create omission uses none; receive omission means none; update omission retains the current mode. Updates affect new root turns, while existing turns and their subagents keep their mode. auto_review reviews eligible actions and denies manual approval fallbacks. No local approval/action runner is added. Removed spending DTOs/fields never map to review or serialize in current requests; historical received spending data can remain opaque extras. AgentServiceTierParam.ultrafast passes every duplicated request validator; future unknown request tiers still reject. Model/tier eligibility and pricing remain service-owned.

AgentSessionAgentUpdate.tools replaces the list: omission retains, null/[] clears, maximum 16384. Function/MCP changes apply on the next model call and built-ins by the next turn. Post-creation updates admit model/reasoning/serviceTier/tools; context overrides belong to saved configuration or session creation. AgentTool.automations()/AgentSessionTool.automations() enable the server's scheduled-follow-up tool; they do not invoke an automation locally.

Session list metadata uses deepObject metadata[key]=value with exact AND matching, at most 16 pairs, keys 1–64 code points and values up to 512. Empty filters emit no pairs. Malformed Unicode rejects privately before authentication; valid strings stay exact. Retain filters/order/agent/cursor while paginating; filter visibility can lag metadata updates. Requests still force agents=v1.

Hosted Artifact SDK/document skills are server-image capabilities. Existing environment creation/template flows prewarm before session attachment; environment and session lifetimes remain independent. See the settings, environment and artifact examples.

- [agent_settings_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/agent_settings_example.dart): Offline context settings, independent review/tools updates, ultrafast and metadata filters; no model execution or compute charges.

## Scheduled Agent automations

client.agents.automations exposes create/list/retrieve/update/delete/pause/resume; .invocations exposes create/list/retrieve. CreateAgentAutomationRequest.once uses future Unix seconds; .periodic uses a five-field cron expression and IANA timezone. AgentAutomationTarget.newSession takes exactly one inline agent or agentId, an environment and a required message array. .existingSession takes a sessionId and instructions. Target and metadata updates replace the complete supplied field; omission retains it, and top-level metadata:{} clears it while null is invalid. Stored target type, creator binding, scheduling state and timing validity are service-owned; the client performs no hidden reads, clock checks or cron interpretation.

Create/update/pause/resume do not invoke work immediately. .invocations.create explicitly queues a manual delivery, even while paused, without changing the schedule or consuming a one-time scheduled run. Invocation completed means delivery was accepted, not Agent work finished; use sessionId to observe session events separately. Queued records can have null sessionId. Preserve scheduledAt, source snapshots, skipReason and error independently. Once-schedule completed means that schedule finished. Pause/delete do not cancel work already accepted by a session, and delete does not delete target sessions.

Both lists return one ID-cursor page, with required nullable firstId/lastId. Preserve order/limit/session filters when requesting after; stop or report a missing/repeated cursor when hasMore rather than looping. All ten operations force agents=v1 and reuse ordinary authentication, HTTP, cancellation and error policy. Pause/resume/manual invocation send no JSON body. New received target/Agent/environment models distinguish saved configuration from an active provisioned session and preserve required nullable fields plus finite immutable future data.

## Live files and published artifacts

client.agents.environments.files.create/list use existing file_id or standard-base64 inline configs directly. Live pages require object:page and nullable next; advance page with identical path/limit/order. client.agents.sessions.artifacts.list/retrieve/delete/download/downloadStream preserve immutable session/environment/turn ownership, original hosted path, size and publication timestamp. Artifact pages use after/lastId and nullable environment filter, with required nullable firstId/lastId. Null query values are omitted. All routes force agents=v1; byte downloads force octet-stream and remove Content-Type, preserve NUL/non-UTF8/empty bytes, use no JSON/text decoding or replay/interceptors, and borrow injected transports. Distinct factory transports are owned. Local abort/cancel releases only observation/download; no session action, delete or local filesystem path is chosen. Published completed-hosted-turn outputs survive environment expiry; unpublished outputs may not survive cancellation/deletion. Retain downloads before session deletion. Artifact deletion leaves live files intact. Canonical metadata sizes have no upper cap; guide file-reference/publication limits remain service-owned. Subagent inspection is available through the child resource; helpers retain deferred tracking.

## Child inspection and history

client.agents.sessions.subagents.list/retrieve, .items.list, .turns.list/retrieve and .turns.items.list inspect service-owned child state. All six GETs force agents=v1 and retain normal auth/project/HTTP/abort policy with opaque nested IDs. ID lists use limit1–100/order/exclusive after, required nullable firstId/lastId and null-query omission. AgentSessionSubagentList is the exact inline list response, not a new canonical schema name. All 63 named closure contracts are reused unchanged, including all 17 history branches and full turn error/usage/timestamps. Child name/instructions/closedAt are required nullable; received instructions preserve output_text/encrypted_content and preview placeholders. OpenedAt remains stable on service resume while closedAt becomes null; reading does not create this transition. Root coordinator history differs from child and child-turn history. No child create/resume/interrupt/close endpoint, independent worker, permissions or automatic tool/history replay is added. Finite future values remain deeply owned, malformed known fields fail privately, and provider/connector/response-stream failures are guarded only at the six new GET origins while local HTTP/parse/timeout/abort classes retain their existing policy. Original causes remain explicit; diagnostic messages omit private payloads. Borrowed clients remain caller-owned. The HTTP/2 evaluation is complete; transport adoption, helpers, and later parity remain deferred.

## Optional

- [Package directory](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/tree/main/packages/openai_dart): Source tree, pubspec, and package-local files.

**Total: ~149.0k tokens**

## Responses WebSocket sessions

`ResponsesWebSocketSession(connection, limits: ResponsesWebSocketLimits(...))` opts into bounded lane routing and final-response collection. Register `session.lane('planner')` (or `lane()` for the default) before sending. Lane `create(request, generate: false)` warms context; continue explicitly with the terminal response ID. A stream ID routes events, not ancestry. `getFinalResponse()` returns completed/failed/incomplete responses and fills omitted/null terminal output from finalized items; explicit empty output remains empty. `receive(abortTrigger: ...)` and `getFinalResponse(abortTrigger: ...)` allow one consumer, retain partial state on cancellation and resume on the same lane. Own-lane overflow fails only that lane; shared pressure fails the largest queued lane. Budgets count canonical UTF-8 parsed JSON, excluding wire whitespace and transport/parse overhead. Session close detaches the reader and leaves the caller-owned connection open; lane IDs remain reserved on that connection. Recovery-enabled connections are currently rejected. No automatic tool execution, continuation, replay or application-specific structured-output parsing is performed.

`ConfigurationUpdateItem.text` uses `ConfigurationUpdateText` with plain text or JSON Schema. Omission preserves the format, explicit null is rejected on the wire, and `const ConfigurationUpdateText.plainText()` resets it. JSON object mode is unsupported. Local parser/output-type metadata never enters API JSON. Stored Responses/Conversations and Live contextual input expose the same typed format contract. Before advancing a store=false source after forking, wait for the fork lane's `response.in_progress`; standalone compaction instead starts a new chain with the entire returned window plus new input.

## Typed reasoning replay

Use `ReasoningItem.toInput()` to snapshot completed returned reasoning into `ReasoningInputItem`, accepted by `ResponseInput.items` and `Item.fromJson`/`fromResourceJson`. Canonical input requires `id` and `summary` (which may be empty), optional reasoning_text content maps, optional nullable encrypted_content, status and beta agent metadata. Preserve item order and the accompanying assistant/tool history, then append application-produced function outputs. No tool execution or reasoning generation is automatic. Use finalized streamed items because added encrypted state may be partial. Input content/status reject explicit null; encrypted content preserves omitted/null/value through hasEncryptedContent and copy semantics. Output retains existing raw-content tolerance and const construction, gains status and independent copies, includes content in equality/hash and redacts payload diagnostics. New Item variants require exhaustive-switch updates. DeepSeek supports plaintext reasoning input but not summaries/encrypted reasoning; raw input remains available for provider-specific shapes. Public examples use synthetic fixtures and do not establish live provider acceptance.

## Voice WebSocket recovery

`LiveReconnectOptions` and `RealtimeReconnectOptions` require an explicit preparation callback. Default `maxQueueBytes: 0` rejects sends during recovery; positive budgets retain only never-attempted frames with strict first-frame accounting. Queued text/binary frames keep their kind and immutable payload. On a fresh socket, restore application state then `flushPending()`, or detach with `takePending()`. Live primary/fork connections reset startup state and require fresh `start(...)` acknowledgment before flushing. Realtime and Translation follow a manual pending policy with a lifetime retry budget; Translation support follows Python where Node differs. Live retries are bounded per interruption. No automatic startup, history, audio or attempted-write replay. Final `recovery.done` includes immutable unsent frames independently of observers. Browser custom headers are rejected; use WebRTC or a backend proxy.

- [websocket_recovery_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/websocket_recovery_example.dart): Local Realtime recovery and explicit state reconciliation, no API charges.

## Native Live Decisions

Configure LiveDecisionsDelegationParam/UpdateParam with native model/questions and optional acknowledgementDelayMs (0–800). LiveDecisionTriggerInputParam selects session.input_transcript.delta or session.output_transcript.delta, independently of delegation. At most two triggers, one per direction; omit updates to retain them or [] to disable. LiveDecisionQuestion and LiveDecisionInstructions preserve Live-specific text/image/JSON rules; native groups require 1–64, independently of standalone Decisions 1–400. FromDecisionQuestion convenience adapts existing criteria without imposing standalone bounds on native decoding.

LiveDecisionInputItemParam supports four role-specific message shapes and function/custom history; stored items require IDs. Send LiveDecisionItemCreateParam/DeleteParam to manage shared state; these do not change voice context or start evaluation. LiveDecisionCreateParam requires a unique 1–256-character eventId. LiveDecisionEvent wraps typed LiveDecisionCompleted and exposes native DecisionResponse through typedDecision, with immutable full wire data. Four required nullable correlation fields distinguish delegation from trigger/source deltas. Keep received order and correlate sourceEventId; results can arrive out of order and are not automatically reordered or applied. When filtering WebRTC events, allow decision.event and each configured source transcript event. Wait for session.updated/item.created before dependent work. Decisions delegation replies can use session.commentary.append with their delegation ID; native Responses commands still require Responses delegation. No tools/actions are executed automatically.

- [live_decisions_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/live_decisions_example.dart): Offline native delegation and one transcript trigger with shared items, acknowledged updates, explicit finalization and zero API cost.
